guide.title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
guide.text: Wheat Field with Cypresses by Vincent van Gogh was made in Saint-Rémy in the summer heat. He wrote to his brother about it and later made copies for his family.

guide.title: Young Woman with a Water Pitcher
guide.text: Young Woman with a Water Pitcher by Johannes Vermeer is about a washing ritual. It was the first of his works to reach America, honoring sacredness in daily home life.

sources.title: Young Woman with a Water Pitcher

guide.title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
guide.text: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer by Rembrandt van Rijn was for a Sicilian collector who let him choose the subject. It endures as a meditation on fame and wisdom.

guide.title: The Harvesters
guide.text: The Harvesters by Pieter Bruegel the Elder was part of a seasons series for a merchant dining room. It honors peasant workers and their harmony with nature and seasonal bounty.

sources.title: Pieter Bruegel the Elder - The Harvesters - The Metropolitan Museum of Art

guide.title: The Death of Socrates
guide.text: The Death of Socrates by Jacques Louis David is about choosing death over giving up beliefs. It became a landmark call to resist unjust authority before the French Revolution.

guide.title: The Card Players
guide.text: The Card Players by Paul Cézanne began a series of five paintings. Made with local farmhands who posed for him, it honors Provençal dignity and points toward modernism.
